description: Symbolic and numeric geometric regions: predefined shapes, implicit and parametric regions, boolean combinations and transformations, discretization into meshes, measures such as area and volume, and computational geometry constructions like convex hulls, Delaunay triangulations and Voronoi diagrams.

tools.name: RegionMember
tools.description: Tests whether a point lies in a region, or returns a reusable RegionMemberFunction when no point is given. It works for symbolic shapes, implicit regions and meshes alike. Use it for point-in-polygon tests, filtering and rejection sampling.
tools.notes: Building the RegionMemberFunction once is far faster than calling RegionMember[reg, pt] repeatedly.

tools.name: RegionDistance
tools.description: Gives the shortest distance from a point to a region, or a reusable distance function. Points inside the region have distance zero. Use it for clearance checks, collision proximity and distance fields.
tools.notes: SignedRegionDistance returns negative values inside the region, which is useful for level-set methods.

tools.name: SignedRegionDistance
tools.description: Gives the distance from a point to the boundary of a region, negative inside and positive outside. This signed form is what level-set and implicit-surface methods need. It accepts the same region types as RegionDistance.

tools.name: RegionMeasure
tools.description: Computes the measure of a region: length for curves, area for surfaces and volume for solids, according to its intrinsic dimension. An explicit dimension can be requested. Use it as the general-purpose size computation.

tools.name: Area
tools.description: Computes the area of a two-dimensional region or surface, symbolically when possible. It accepts polygons, disks, implicit regions and meshes. Use it when the region is genuinely two-dimensional.

tools.name: Volume
tools.description: Computes the volume of a three-dimensional region, symbolically where possible and numerically otherwise. It accepts solids, implicit regions and 3D meshes. Use it for capacity, mass and integration setup.
tools.example:
Volume[Ball[{0, 0, 0}, 3]]
Volume[ImplicitRegion[x^2 + y^2 + z^2 <= 1 && z >= 0, {x, y, z}]]

tools.name: Perimeter
tools.description: Computes the perimeter, that is the total boundary length, of a two-dimensional region. For 3D regions use Area of the boundary instead. It works on polygons, disks and meshes.

tools.name: RegionCentroid
tools.description: Computes the geometric centroid (center of mass of uniform density) of a region. It works for curves, surfaces and solids. Use it for shape descriptors, balancing and alignment.

tools.name: RegionBounds
tools.description: Returns the axis-aligned bounding box of a region as a list of coordinate ranges. It is the quickest way to size a plot range or a grid over a region. A "Bounds" or "Intersection" specification controls the exact convention.

tools.name: RegionNearest
tools.description: Returns the point of a region closest to a given point, or a reusable nearest-point function. It is the projection operator onto the region. Use it for snapping, constraint projection and closest-feature queries.

tools.name: ImplicitRegion
tools.description: Defines a region by inequalities and equations in the coordinate variables. It supports full boolean logic, so complicated domains are easy to express. Most region functions accept it directly, discretizing internally when needed.
tools.example:
reg = ImplicitRegion[x^2 + y^2 <= 4 && y >= x^2 - 1, {x, y}];
{Area[reg], RegionPlot[reg]}

tools.name: ParametricRegion
tools.description: Defines a region as the image of a parameter domain under a coordinate map. It represents curves, surfaces and solids that are naturally parameterized. Region functions handle it symbolically where possible.
tools.usage:
ParametricRegion[{fx, fy}, {{u, a, b}}]
ParametricRegion[expr, params]

tools.name: MeshRegion
tools.description: Represents a region as an explicit mesh of points and cells such as lines, triangles and tetrahedra. It is the discrete representation that most numeric region operations use internally. Build one with DiscretizeRegion or directly from coordinates and cells.
tools.notes: MeshCells, MeshCoordinates and MeshPrimitives extract the underlying structure.

tools.name: BoundaryMeshRegion
tools.description: Represents a solid region by its boundary mesh, so that the interior is implied rather than tessellated. It is more compact than a full volume mesh and supports volume and membership queries. Use it for closed surfaces imported from CAD or STL files.

tools.name: DiscretizeRegion
tools.description: Converts a symbolic region into a MeshRegion of cells filling its interior. Mesh resolution is controlled by MaxCellMeasure and related options. Use it before numeric integration, FEM or rendering.
tools.example:
reg = ImplicitRegion[x^2 + y^2 <= 1, {x, y}];
DiscretizeRegion[reg, MaxCellMeasure -> 0.01]

tools.name: BoundaryDiscretizeRegion
tools.description: Converts a region into a BoundaryMeshRegion representing only its boundary surface. It is cheaper than full discretization when only the surface matters. Use it for rendering, STL export and boundary-element methods.

tools.name: RegionUnion
tools.description: Forms the union of several regions, producing a region representing all points in any of them. It works on symbolic shapes and on meshes. Use it to assemble complex domains from simple parts.

tools.name: RegionIntersection
tools.description: Forms the intersection of several regions, the set of points common to all of them. It is a boolean operation on geometry rather than on predicates. Use it for overlap analysis and constrained domains.

tools.name: RegionDifference
tools.description: Subtracts one or more regions from another, leaving the points in the first but not in the rest. It is the geometric analogue of Complement. Use it to cut holes and carve features.
tools.notes: RegionSymmetricDifference gives the points in exactly one of two regions.

tools.name: TransformedRegion
tools.description: Applies a geometric transformation to a region, producing the transformed region. Any TransformationFunction such as rotation, scaling or an affine map can be used. Use it to place and orient parts of an assembly.

tools.name: ConvexHullMesh
tools.description: Computes the convex hull of a set of points as a mesh region, in two or three dimensions. The result supports all region operations including measure and membership. Use it for shape bounding, collision proxies and outlier envelopes.
tools.notes: ConvexHullRegion returns a symbolic region rather than a mesh.

tools.name: ConvexHullRegion
tools.description: Returns the convex hull of a set of points as a symbolic region, which can be combined with other regions exactly. It avoids the discretization implicit in a mesh. Use it when exact geometric reasoning is needed.

tools.name: DelaunayMesh
tools.description: Computes the Delaunay triangulation of a point set as a mesh region, maximizing the minimum angle of the triangles. It is the standard triangulation for interpolation and finite elements. Works in 2D and 3D.

tools.name: VoronoiMesh
tools.description: Computes the Voronoi diagram of a point set, partitioning space into cells of points closest to each site. It is the geometric dual of the Delaunay triangulation. Use it for nearest-facility analysis, territory maps and spatial statistics.

tools.name: TriangulateMesh
tools.description: Retriangulates a mesh region into simplices, refining it to a requested cell size. It turns polygonal or coarse meshes into well-shaped triangle or tetrahedron meshes. Use it before finite-element computation or smooth rendering.

tools.name: MeshCells
tools.description: Returns the cells of a mesh region at a given dimension, as index lists into the mesh coordinates. Dimension 0 gives points, 1 lines, 2 faces and 3 solids. Use it to inspect or export mesh connectivity.

tools.name: MeshCoordinates
tools.description: Returns the coordinates of all points in a mesh region as a list of vectors. Together with MeshCells it fully describes the mesh. Use it to convert a mesh into arrays for external tools.

tools.name: MeshPrimitives
tools.description: Returns the cells of a mesh as explicit geometric primitives such as Point, Line, Triangle or Tetrahedron with actual coordinates. Unlike MeshCells it resolves the indices. Use it to render or measure individual cells.

tools.name: RegionBoundary
tools.description: Returns the boundary of a region as a region of one lower dimension. For a disk it gives a circle and for a solid it gives its surface. Use it to compute surface areas and to apply boundary conditions.

tools.name: RandomPoint
tools.description: Generates uniformly distributed random points inside a region. It handles symbolic regions and meshes, using rejection or direct sampling as appropriate. Use it for Monte Carlo integration and randomized testing.

tools.name: Ball
tools.description: Represents a solid ball of given center and radius in any number of dimensions. In two dimensions it coincides with a disk. Use it as an exact region for measures, membership and boolean operations.
tools.usage:
Ball[]
Ball[c, r]
Ball[{c1, c2, ...}, r]

tools.name: Ellipsoid
tools.description: Represents a solid ellipsoid with given center and semi-axis lengths or a full covariance-style matrix. It is the natural region for confidence ellipsoids of multivariate distributions. Measures and membership are exact.

tools.name: Simplex
tools.description: Represents the simplex with given vertices, the general triangle/tetrahedron in any dimension. It is the basic building block of meshes. Use it for finite elements and barycentric computations.

tools.name: Triangle
tools.description: Represents a filled triangle with three given vertices, in 2D or 3D. It is both a graphics primitive and an exact region. Use it for mesh faces and simple polygonal geometry.

tools.name: RegularPolygon
tools.description: Represents a regular polygon with a given number of sides, optionally with a specified center, circumradius and rotation. It is both a drawable primitive and a measurable region. Use it for tilings, gears and symmetric shapes.
tools.usage:
RegularPolygon[n]
RegularPolygon[r, n]
RegularPolygon[{x, y}, {r, theta}, n]

tools.name: Annulus
tools.description: Represents the region between two concentric circles or spheres. It is the natural shape for rings, washers and shells. Measures, membership and boolean operations all work exactly.

tools.name: InfinitePlane
tools.description: Represents an unbounded plane through given points or through a point with a normal direction. It is useful as a slicing surface and as a constraint. Many region operations accept it despite being unbounded.
tools.notes: Hyperplane, InfiniteLine and HalfLine are the related unbounded primitives.

tools.name: RegionQ
tools.description: Tests whether an expression is a valid geometric region. It is the type guard used when writing generic geometry code. BoundedRegionQ and RegionDimension give further structural information.

tools.name: RegionDimension
tools.description: Gives the intrinsic dimension of a region, for example 1 for a curve and 2 for a surface. RegionEmbeddingDimension gives the dimension of the ambient space instead. Use both to reason about which measure applies.

tools.name: NearestFunction
tools.description: Represents a precomputed nearest-neighbour search structure returned by Nearest. Applying it to a query point is much faster than rebuilding the search each time. Use it in loops and inside simulations.
